languageModelTools.name: rustyRefactor_extract_to_module
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Extracts selected Rust code from a source file and creates a new module file with:
- Intelligent import handling
- Impl block preservation
- Automatic parent module registration
- rust-analyzer validation

This tool enforces Rust conventions and ensures only clean, compiling code is delivered.

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:
1) modulePath must be RELATIVE to workspace root, starting with 'src/'.
   - DO NOT include workspace root path.
   - Example (CORRECT): 'src/controllers/ads/facebook/facebook_ads.rs'
   - Example (WRONG): '/home/user/project/src/...'
   - The 'src/' folder ALREADY EXISTS; do not try to create it.
2) Module structure must follow 'one module per folder'.
   - Each module file must be in its own folder with a mod.rs.
   - Example: 'src/controllers/ads/facebook/' contains both 'mod.rs' AND 'facebook_ads.rs'.
   - Flat structures like 'src/controllers/ads/facebook_ads.rs' are REJECTED with error.
3) moduleName must be snake_case (lowercase_with_underscores).

The tool automatically:
- Validates extracted code compiles with rust-analyzer (3 auto-fix attempts)
- Creates missing folders and mod.rs files
- Removes extracted code from source (no comments)
- Normalizes paths using built-in Utils.extractWorkspaceRoot()
- Applies all changes atomically using WorkspaceEdit API

Returns structured JSON with success status, extracted items, and import statements.
Tool will ABORT if validation fails after auto-fix attempts.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Extract Rust code to a new module with validation and auto-fixing

sourceFilePath.description: The absolute file path of the Rust source file containing the code to extract. Must be a .rs file.

startLine.description: The starting line number of the code to extract (1-based, inclusive). Should point to the beginning of a complete Rust item (function, struct, impl block, etc.).

endLine.description: The ending line number of the code to extract (1-based, inclusive). Should point to the end of a complete Rust item.

moduleName.description: The name of the module to create. REQUIRED FORMAT: snake_case (lowercase with underscores). Examples: 'facebook_ads', 'user_service', 'email_repository'. Will be validated and rejected if not snake_case.

modulePath.description: CRITICAL: Must be RELATIVE path starting with 'src/' - DO NOT include workspace root. The 'src/' directory already exists in the workspace. REQUIRED STRUCTURE: Module must be in its own folder with mod.rs. CORRECT EXAMPLES: 'src/controllers/ads/facebook/facebook_ads.rs' (creates folder 'facebook/' with mod.rs + facebook_ads.rs), 'src/models/user/user_repository.rs'. WRONG EXAMPLES: 'src/controllers/ads/facebook_ads.rs' (flat structure - REJECTED), '/home/user/project/src/...' (absolute path - will be normalized but avoid). Folders are auto-created. For RustyRoad projects use: src/controllers/, src/models/, src/services/, src/middleware/, src/helpers/, src/utils/. If omitted, defaults to 'src/{moduleName}.rs'.

functionName.description: Optional: Name of a specific function/struct/enum to extract using symbol matching (more reliable than line numbers). If provided, the tool will find the symbol by name and extract it, using line numbers only as fallback.

languageModelTools.name: rustyRefactor_analyze_rust_code
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Analyzes a selection of Rust code and provides detailed information about its structure, dependencies, and components. This tool should be used when you need to understand what a piece of Rust code contains before refactoring or when gathering information for code review. It detects and reports: all functions with their visibility and generic parameters, all structs with field counts and visibility, all enums with variant counts, all traits, implementation blocks (impl) including trait implementations, whether the code is inside an impl block, all used types and traits, all imports (use statements), overall visibility level, and presence of generic parameters. The tool is useful for determining if code is suitable for extraction to a module and understanding its dependencies. File paths must be absolute paths. Line numbers are 1-based and inclusive.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Analyze Rust code structure, dependencies, and components

filePath.description: The absolute file path of the Rust source file to analyze. Must be a .rs file.

startLine.description: The starting line number to analyze (1-based, inclusive).

endLine.description: The ending line number to analyze (1-based, inclusive).

languageModelTools.name: rustyRefactor_srp_refactor
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Automatically refactors a Rust file into cohesive modules following the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) with a configurable line limit per module. This tool uses an LLM to intelligently plan how to split symbols into groups based on cohesion and responsibility, then executes the extraction plan automatically.

Workflow:
1. Analyzes the file to discover all symbols (structs, enums, traits, functions, impl blocks)
2. Sends the full symbol map to an LLM which plans SRP-based groupings
3. Extracts each group to its own module folder (one module per folder convention)
4. Creates mod.rs files with re-exports
5. Suggests missing imports using FFI (nativeBridge)
6. Validates with rust-analyzer

The LLM ensures:
- Each module has a single, clear responsibility
- Structs and their impl blocks stay together
- Tightly coupled helpers stay with their parent symbol
- Each module stays within the line limit

Just provide the file path. Optionally set maxLinesPerModule (default 50) and targetDirectory.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Auto-split a Rust file into SRP-compliant modules with LLM-powered planning

filePath.description: The absolute path to the Rust file to refactor into SRP modules

maxLinesPerModule.description: Maximum non-blank lines per extracted module (default: 50). The LLM will group symbols to stay within this limit.

targetDirectory.description: Optional: Base directory for extracted modules. Defaults to RustyRoad conventions (src/models, src/services, etc.). Each module gets its own subfolder.

autoFixImports.description: Optional: Whether to auto-fix missing imports after extraction (default: true)

languageModelTools.name: rustyRefactor_refactor_file
languageModelTools.modelDescription: High-level orchestration tool that automatically refactors an entire Rust file. This tool automatically: 1) Analyzes the file to discover extractable symbols, 2) Extracts each symbol to appropriate modules based on RustyRoad conventions, 3) Suggests missing imports using existing TypeScript utilities, 4) Returns a complete refactoring plan. The tool leverages the extract_rust_module and analyze_rust tools internally and uses built-in Utils class functions for path normalization and string manipulation. LLM doesn't need to do ANY work - just call this tool with the file path and optionally specify target directory or symbols to extract. The tool handles all the complexity of symbol matching, module creation, and import fixing automatically.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Automatically refactor an entire Rust file with analysis, extraction, and import fixing

filePath.description: The absolute path to the Rust file to refactor

targetDirectory.description: Optional: Target directory for extracted modules (defaults to RustyRoad conventions). Examples: 'src/models', 'src/services', 'src/controllers'

symbolsToExtract.description: Optional: Specific symbols to extract (if empty, extracts all public items)

autoFixImports.description: Optional: Whether to auto-fix missing imports (default: true)

rustyRefactor.rustyRoadMode.description: Enable RustyRoad-specific conventions (suggests controllers, models, services, etc.)

rustyRefactor.addModuleDocComments.description: Add documentation comments to extracted modules

rustyRefactor.integrationWithRustAnalyze.description: Integrate with rust-analyzer for better type detection and unused import cleanup

rustyRefactor.rustAnalyzerValidationTime.description: Maximum time (ms) to wait for rust-analyzer diagnostics to appear while validating extracted modules. Increase for slower systems.

rustyRefactor.rustAnalyzerValidationPoll.description: Polling interval (ms) used when waiting for rust-analyzer diagnostics to change. Lower for faster detection, higher to reduce resource usage.

rustyRefactor.aiAutoDocumentation.description: Automatically generate AI-powered documentation for extracted modules using GitHub Copilot

rustyRefactor.aiAskEachTime.description: Ask before generating AI documentation each time (if aiAutoDocumentation is false)

rustyRefactor.aiPreferredModel.description: Preferred AI model for documentation generation (format: vendor/family). Use 'Rusty Refactor: Select AI Model' command to choose.

rustyRefactor.aiFastModel.description: Fast AI model used for validation and summaries (format: vendor/family). Uses models matching 'mini/flash/haiku' automatically if not set. Set to a small fast model like 'copilot/gpt-4o-mini' for faster validation.

rustyRefactor.searchDepth.description: Maximum directory depth for file search

rustyRefactor.useCodetether.description: Use Codetether as the AI backend instead of VS Code built-in language models

rustyRefactor.codetetherModel.description: Default model name for Codetether (e.g. zai/glm-5). Leave empty for automatic selection.

rustyRefactor.codetetherBinaryPath.description: Path to the codetether binary. Defaults to 'codetether' (must be on PATH).

rustyRefactor.codetetherChatTransport.description: Chat transport. Use 'run' for codetether run -c.

rustyRefactor.codetetherA2AServerUrl.description: Optional URL of a remote Codetether A2A server to use for model discovery and chat (e.g. http://localhost:8000). Useful when port-forwarding a cluster-hosted a2a-server.
